items.title: A2A Java SDK send client credentials under server-controlled HTTP header name, enabling leakage via redirect
items.description:
*Impact.** A malicious or compromised A2A agent can cause the client's API key credential to be forwarded to an arbitrary third-party server. The agent serves an AgentCard with an `APIKeySecurityScheme` specifying a custom header name, then responds with an HTTP redirect. The JDK HttpClient follows the redirect and forwards the custom header containing the credential, since only the standard `Authorization` header may be stripped on cross-origin redirects.

**Where.** `client/transport/spi/src/main/java/org/a2aproject/sdk/client/transport/spi/interceptors/auth/AuthInterceptor.java:69` in `intercept`

items.title: Pillow: Out-of-bounds access in _imagingmorph on a zero-width image
items.description:
### Summary
A PPM or PGM file can declare a width of 0, which Pillow accepts, producing an image of size `(0, N)`. Passing that image to `ImageMorph.MorphOp.apply()` makes the native morphology code index a row buffer at `outrow[width - 1]`, which is `outrow[-1]` when the width is 0. The process crashes.

### Details
The PPM parser reads width and height with no lower-bound check:

- `src/PIL/PpmImagePlugin.py:119`

The native `apply()` writes the row edges with no guard that the width is positive:

`match()` and `get_on_pixels()` use the same edge-indexing pattern.

items.description:
## Summary

A small attacker-supplied TIFF can be opened and loaded normally, then reach an out-of-bounds read when an application saves it back to TIFF with retained metadata. The fixed reproducer is a 1×1, 16-bit grayscale, PackBits-compressed TIFF containing tag 320 (ColorMap) with **768 SHORT values**: three zero-filled planes of 256 entries each. No Python object is forged and no metadata is injected after loading.

Pillow's TIFF encoder allocates **768 × 2 = 1536 bytes**, then passes three plane pointers separated by 256 SHORT entries to libtiff. With `BitsPerSample = 16`, libtiff instead expects **65536 SHORT values per plane** and attempts a **131072-byte read** from a plane pointer. Existing ASAN observations identify a heap-buffer-overflow READ crossing the 1536-byte allocation made in `PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew`.

items.description:
### Summary

Pillow's libImaging `_decodeTile` decoder, used to decode tiled TIFF images, allocates a per-tile buffer using `realloc(state->buffer, TIFFTileSize(tiff))`. After each `TIFFReadTile` it then iterates `tile_y` from 0 up to `current_tile_length` and calls the configured row unpacker (here `copy4`) with the source pointer `state->buffer + tile_y * row_byte_size`. When libtiff returns a `tile_bytes_size` smaller than the worst-case `row_byte_size * tile_length`, the inner stride-and-copy loop walks past the realloc'd region and `copy4` performs a 1024-byte `memcpy` that reads up to `(tile_length-1) * row_byte_size + row_byte_size` bytes from a buffer sized only to `tile_bytes_size`. The supplied PoC TIFF triggers a 1024-byte over-read exactly 0 bytes past a 196608-byte allocation. ## Summary

`JpegImageFile.draft()` — which `Image.thumbnail()` calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks `self._size` and the tile extents to match, so `_setimage()` allocates a single-row decode buffer of `ceil(W/s)` samples. `ImagingJpegDecode()` sets `cinfo.scale_num`/`scale_denom`, calls `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and then reads scanlines into that buffer without ever comparing `cinfo.output_width`, `cinfo.output_height` or `cinfo.out_color_components` against `state->xsize`, `state->ysize` and `state->bits`.

items.title: markdown-it: Quadratic-time rendering of a single multi-line link reference definition with default options (regression since 14.0)
items.description:
### Summary

A link reference definition whose label or title is never closed is O(n²) in markdown-it 15.0.2 with default options. Continuation lines are pulled lazily with str += lineContent in src/rules_block/reference.ts, and the subsequent charCodeAt and slice calls flatten the V8 cons-string, copying everything collected so far; this runs before the rule decides the definition is invalid. It is a regression introduced by PR #1004 in 14.0.0: 13.0.2 processed a 313 KB input in 125 ms, while every version since takes about 11 seconds on the same input. At the sizes below, 200 KB takes 3.6 seconds, 400 KB takes 18.1 seconds, and 800 KB takes 74.0 seconds, which is roughly 4–5× per doubling. No options are required to trigger it.

items.description:
### Summary

With `html: true`, markdown-it takes quadratic time to parse repeated unterminated HTML constructs inside a paragraph. This affects HTML comments (`<!--`), processing instructions (`<?`), declarations (`<!A`), and CDATA sections (`<![CDATA[`).

An attacker-controlled input of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for seconds or tens of seconds. The default configuration has HTML disabled, but the `commonmark` preset enables it.

The issue was reported against the published `markdown-it@15.0.2` package on Node.js 20 and reproduced on the current source with Node.js 24.16.0.

### Details

`src/rules_inline/text.ts` treats `<` as a terminator, causing the inline parser to attempt the HTML rule at successive HTML construct openers.

items.title: MCP  TypeScript server SDK: Shared transport or server instances delivered one HTTP client's messages to another
items.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, an MCP server reached over HTTP could deliver one client's responses and notifications to another client. This happened when clients shared one stateless transport, or one `McpServer` or `Server` instance.

Messages were matched to a connection by JSON-RPC `id` alone. SDK clients number requests from 0, so ids collide in normal use.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if more than one client can reach your HTTP endpoint and your code creates the transport or the server once at startup, instead of once per request or per session. Until this release, the README examples of `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`, `express`, `fastify` and `node` showed that pattern.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0.

Not affected:

- `createMcpHandler()` with a factory that builds a new server on every call
- stdio servers
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.26.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during validation
items.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, servers put no limit on how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request. One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with `JavaScript heap out of memory`.

No credentials are needed, unless you authenticate requests before they reach the SDK.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if clients you do not fully trust can reach your server over HTTP. The risk is highest for `McpServer` tools whose input contains an array or a record. stdio-only servers are not affected.

Affected versions:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.3.0 through 1.31.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0

### Fix
Upgrade to:

- 1.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later
- 2.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or later

**Upgrading alone changes nothing.** The patched versions add an `M

items.title: AIOHTTP: Absolute-form request targets can spoof Request.scheme
items.description:
### Summary

An attacker sending an absolute-form request can spoof the scheme used.

### Impact

If user code depends on the `Request.scheme` attribute for anything security related, an attacker may be able to circumvent this logic, tricking the application into thinking a connection is encrypted when it is not, or vice versa.

### Workaround

A WAF rule to reject absolute-form requests (legitimate requests should only use this form for proxies).

items.title: AIOHTTP: Cookie from subdomain can remove Host-Only Scope from existing cookies
items.description:
### Summary

A subdomain can remove the Host-Only flag from an existing cookie to a parent domain.

### Impact

A user accessing untrusted subdomains could see their Host-Only protections stripped from cookies. Given most usecases won't reflect these cookies to a browser, the impact is limited.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Connector pool exhaustion via Max-Age overflow
items.description:
### Summary

An overflow in Max-Age processing can skip closing a connection.

### Impact

An attacker may be able to exhaust the connection pool temporarily, until garbage collection resolves the connections.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request smuggling
items.description:
### Summary

The pure Python parser is vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling attack.

### Impact

If users are using the Python parser (`AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS`, or not a standard wheel installed), then an application may be vulnerable to a request smuggling attack.

### Workaround

Switch to the default C parser.

items.title: AIOHTTP: File descriptor exhaustion in multipart requests
items.description:
### Summary

An attacker can exhaust file descriptors with specially crafted multipart requests.

### Impact

If a handler uses `Request.post()`, it may be possible for an attacker to use an unlimited number of file descriptors, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion.

items.title: launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary command execution for some editors
items.description:
### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file overwrites or command execution.

### Impact

#### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the user is using WSL

#### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affecte

items.title: launch-editor: `fs.existsSync()` existence check can be bypassed on Windows
items.description:
### Summary

`launch-editor` checked `fs.existsSync(fileName)` before passing a supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass this check with a crafted path ending in `\\..:line:column`. This removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a malicious filename.

Combined with the `%` escaping issue described in [GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv), this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls the file argument.

### Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

### Details

The earlier advisory assumed that `fs.existsSync()` required an attacker-controlled filename to exist. This advisory covers a bypass of that requirement.

A crafted value ending in `\\..:1:1` is interpreted differently by `launch-editor-middleware`, `launch-editor`, and Win

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: Server bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for another service
items.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, the SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check that a token was issued for your server (its audience). Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your HTTP server uses `requireBearerAuth()` or `verifyBearerToken()`, its authorization server also issues tokens for other services, and your `verifyAccessToken()` does not check the token's audience (`aud`) itself.

Affected versions:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.6.0 through 1.31.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/express` 2.0.0 through 2.0.1
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy` 2.0.0 through 2.3.0

### Fix
Upgrade to:

- 1.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later
- 2.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or lat

items.title: uv's bundled CA store trusts an emSign root whose intermediate CA keys are compromised
items.description:
By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the `webpki-root-certs` bundle. Versions before 0.13.4 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to that root have compromised private keys, and the CA has revoked them.

An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

uv 0.13.4 removes the root from its vendored bundle, following `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10. Upgrade to 0.13.4 or later.

items.title: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys
items.description:
Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them. 

An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.

Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

items.title: launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows
items.description:
### Summary

`launch-editor` did not escape `%` on Windows when passing an argument to `cmd`. When an environment variable contained a malicious value, it was possible that that content to be executed.

### Impact

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The user uses Windows
- An attacker can place a file with the malicious filename containing `&` or `%`
- Either of
  - An attacker can inject an environment variable with a malicious value
  - An attacker can add a NTFS alternate data stream to the file placed

### Details

Unlike `.sh` files, `.bat` / `.cmd` files on Windows cannot be called directly using [`child_process.spawn`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/child_process.html#child_processspawncommand-args-options) and requires passing them as an argument of `cmd.exe`. To do so, launch-editor escapes the arguments passed to `cmd.exe`. But `laun

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them
items.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, the experimental tasks feature (`taskStore`) did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one `InMemoryTaskStore` could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

Experimental tasks are deprecated. The 2026-07-28 specification replaced them with a redesigned extension. The best course of action is to stop using them.

### Am I affected?
Only if your HTTP server passes `taskStore` to `McpServer` or `Server`. If `grep -ri taskstore --exclude-dir=node_modules .` finds nothing, you are not affected.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.24.0 through 1.31.0. The 2.x packages are not affected.

### Fix
Upgrade to `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later. Each task is now tied to the session that created it, so a client that starts a new session can no longer reach its earlier tasks.

If you cannot upgrade yet, remove `taskStore`,

items.title: MCP TypeScript client SDK: HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent custom headers and request bodies
items.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, the SDK's HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed redirects to any origin.

If an MCP server or authorization server redirected a request to another origin, that origin received custom request headers (such as an `X-API-Key` set in `requestInit.headers`) and the `mcp-session-id` header. On a `307` or `308` it also received the request body, including OAuth token requests with their `refresh_token` and `client_secret`.

On current runtimes `fetch` already drops the `Authorization` header across origins.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your application uses `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`, `SSEClientTransport`, or the SDK's OAuth client functions such as `auth()`. stdio clients are not affected.

Affected versions:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` all versions through 1.31.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0

items.title: ApostropheCMS: The general public can access @apostrophecms/user objects via a relationship (viewRole is not applied to the general public)
items.description:
### Impact
Even though it is correctly applied to guests, contributors, etc., `viewRole` is not applied to the general public. This means that a secured content type like `@apostrophecms/user` can in theory be accessed.

This is greatly mitigated by the fact that there is no automatic public REST API for any content type. One has to expressly allow it. However, it does mean that developers can make the mistake of setting up a relationship between a content type like a blog post, and `@apostrophecms/user`. This could potentially expose some sensitive information if templates were written poorly, e.g. if they JSON-serialized the entire object. Note that password hashes are NOT affected because they reside in a separate collection.

The public demo project and its various flavors must be updated first because it inadvertently relies on the bug.

ApostropheCMS import-export tar guard misses './..' because it is a literal '../' substring test
ApostropheCMS: Path traversal in uploadfs
items.description:
## Summary
The `uploadfs` library's local storage backend does not validate or sanitize user-supplied paths. The `prefixPath()` helper only strips double slashes (`//`) and the backend performs direct string concatenation (`uploadsPath + path`). An attacker can inject `../` sequences to escape the intended uploads directory, resulting in arbitrary file read, write, and delete on the host filesystem.

---

## Details

items.description:
## Summary

The client-side helper `apos.http.parseQuery()` in ApostropheCMS builds a nested object
from a URL query string without sanitizing the keys `__proto__`, `constructor`, or
`prototype`. Parsing an attacker-controlled query string therefore writes arbitrary
properties onto `Object.prototype` (client-side prototype pollution).

ApostropheCMS's admin UI calls this parser with `window.location.search` on **every
authenticated page load** (the admin context bar's `data()` initializer). Because the admin
UI is built on Vue, a polluted, enumerable property on `Object.prototype` is then picked up
by Vue's standard element-mount routine and written to the DOM as an element property,
turning the prototype pollution into DOM-based XSS in the victim's authenticated session.

items.description:
### Summary
follow-redirects removes sensitive credential headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, and any caller-declared `sensitiveHeaders`) before following a redirect that crosses to a different host or downgrades to a less secure protocol. The removal routine iterates the caller's headers container with `for...in` and matches header names against a filter. This assumes the headers container is a plain object keyed by header names. ### Summary
follow-redirects 1.16.0 introduced the `sensitiveHeaders` option (the fix for CVE-2026-40895 / GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653), which lets an application declare extra header names that must be removed when a redirect crosses to a different host or downgrades protocol. The filter is a single case-insensitive regular expression built by concatenating the declared header names into an alternation after passing each through `escapeRegex`. `escapeRegex` escapes only a partial set of metacharacters and leaves `^`, `|`, `[`, `{`, and `}` unescaped. Header names may legitimately contain `^` and `|` (both are valid RFC 9110 token characters that Node accepts and sends), and for a declared name containing either, the generated pattern can never match the intended header. A denial of service (DoS) vulnerability was identified in `@angular/router` when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled on Node.js (V8).

items.description:
### Summary

`serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time after Hono has already decoded it for routing. A crafted request can be routed as one path and served as another, so middleware mounted on a static prefix does not run for a file under that prefix.

### Details

Hono decodes the request path once before routing. `serveStatic` decoded it again before resolving the file. With a malformed percent-encoded sequence, the first decode leaves part of the path encoded, the router matches the encoded form, and the second decode resolves the real directory. The file is still resolved inside the configured root; this is not a traversal outside it.

items.title: markdown-it: Quadratic complexity in smartquotes with unmatched closing quotes

### Impact

When `typographer: true` is enabled, specially crafted Markdown can cause quadratic processing time in the smartquotes rule, potentially leading to denial of service in applications processing untrusted input.

Many opening double quotes followed by unmatched closing single quotes cause repeated scans of the entire opener stack. The same issue occurs with the quote types reversed.

The default configuration (`typographer: false`) is not affected, but this option is enabled with high probability.

### Reproduction

```js

import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'

const md = new MarkdownIt({ typographer: true })

for (const k of [2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {
  const input = '"a '.repeat(k) + "b' ".repeat(k)
  const start = performance.now()
  md.render(input)
  console.log(input.length, (performance.now() - start).toFixed(1), 'ms')

Repeating one constrained add-key message over an agent connection converts wire bytes into resident tasks and heap at roughly 141x amplification: in our measurement 10.2 MiB of protocol traffic produced ~2,096,120 live tasks and +1,447,856 KiB RSS, while the same traffic sent as unconstrained add-key requests cost +268 KiB. items.description:
### Details

In `russh/src/server/encrypted.rs`, `server_read_auth_request_pk` (0.63.3, around lines 880-990):

* The requested algorithm name (`pubkey_algo`) is read and only used to decode the key: `PublicKeyOrCertificate::decode(&pubkey_algo, &pubkey_key)`. The derived `hash_alg` is then dropped (`PublicKeyOrCertificate::PublicKey { ref key, .. }`).
* The signature blob is decoded (`Signature::decode`) and verified with `Verifier::verify(&pubkey, &buf, &sig)`. `ssh-key` picks the hash from **the signature's own algorithm** (`sig.algorithm()`).
* `pubkey_algo` and `sig.algorithm()` are never compared.

So for an RSA key, the request can say `rsa-sha2-512` while the signature is `ssh-rsa`. The signature is valid for SHA-1, verification succeeds, and `Handler::auth_publickey` is called.

items.title: Mercury: Stored / DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): mr.Markdown renders untrusted content as raw, unsanitized HTML

Mercury turns Jupyter notebooks into shared web apps/dashboards. The `mr.Markdown`

triggered by ordinary, reasonable application code, not by an author mistake.

```python

items.title: agent-router: MCP session resume does not verify the embedded anti-hijacking subject; default Helm seed makes session IDs forgeable
items.description:
## Summary

The MCP proxy's client-facing session ID embeds the authenticated caller's
subject (JWT `sub` claim) specifically as an anti-hijacking discriminator —
matching the Model Context Protocol specification's documented session-hijacking
guidance (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/security_best_practices#session-hijacking).
However, the session-resume path never checks that discriminator against the
current caller's identity, so any client that obtains a session ID (its own or
another user's) can resume that session and act with it — including on
routes with per-user backend sessions. This is aggravated by the official
Helm chart shipping a literal, publicly known default seed
(`"default-insecure-seed"`) for the key that encrypts these session IDs.

items.title: Graphify Fortran extractor: incomplete cpp #include hardening allows arbitrary host-file read/exfiltration when indexing an untrusted repo
items.description:
## Summary

The Fortran extractor's C-preprocessor step (`graphify/extractors/fortran.py`, `_cpp_preprocess`) applies an incomplete `#include` hardening. The `-nostdinc -I /dev/null` flags it relies on (comment "Security (F-007)") do **not** stop a capital-`F` Fortran source file from including **absolute paths** (`#include "/etc/passwd"`) or from **path-traversing out of the corpus** (`#include "../../../../home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa"`). `cpp` always searches the directory of the file being preprocessed for quoted includes and always honours absolute include paths, regardless of `-nostdinc`/`-I`. items.title: Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via /api/kernels
items.description:
Mercury runs a JupyterLab server with **anonymous access by default** (`mercury_app/__main__.py` sets `--IdentityProvider.token=''` when no `--token`/`MERCURY_TOKEN` is given; when tokenless it also sets `--ServerApp.disable_check_xsrf=True`). It relies on a **blocklist** (`mercury_app/block_handler.py` `BLOCKED_PATTERNS`: `/lab`, `/api/terminals`, `/api/shutdown`, `/files`) to keep anonymous users off dangerous Jupyter endpoints.

## The vulnerability

items.title: LoopX serve-status permissive CORS policy exposes control-plane state and private Markdown files
items.description:
## Summary

`loopx serve-status` sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on **every** response,
including its unauthenticated `GET` routes. Because the endpoint is unauthenticated and
bound to a fixed, well-known loopback port, **any website the operator visits can read
LoopX control-plane state and the contents of Markdown files inside every registered goal
repo**, using a plain `fetch()` with no user interaction.

The write endpoints are *not* affected — they are correctly Origin-checked. This report is
strictly about the **read** paths.
